output.summary: The team discussed cost-cutting measures for a remote control design during a project meeting. Initially, the design included 15 buttons, one LCD screen, an advanced chip-on-print, a speech sensor, and kinetic energy for power. Due to budget constraints, they decided to replace kinetic energy with standard batteries and drop the speech recognition feature, which was deemed unreliable and costly. They also reduced the number of buttons by eliminating direct channel access buttons (1-9) in favor of using up/down arrows, saving €4.50. The design was simplified further by replacing multiple buttons with a single integrated scroll-wheel push-button for menu navigation and functionality. The LCD screen was retained for its essential role in providing visual feedback and user interaction. The casing material was switched to hard plastic, which is more cost-effective than wood or rubber, and the design was modified to be singly curved rather than doubly curved to reduce costs. Despite simplifications, concerns were raised about the ease of use of the streamlined interface. The team evaluated the final design using criteria such as technological innovation, usability, and aesthetics, and assigned it a score of approximately 3.1. The final product will be a single-curved, plastic remote with an LCD screen and an integrated scroll-wheel push-button, featuring a special color to maintain a trendy appearance. The meeting concluded with plans to finalize reports and presentations before the deadline.
